Content Limit Campaign title 6 words or fewer Campaign description 50–100 words Use a campaign when you want to explore different parts of the same issue. For example: Campaign: Improving Marin transportation How can we improve bus service? Where do we need safer crossings? How can we improve bike routes? Each question collects its own ideas, comments, and votes. The campaign connects them under one effort. Use a question for one conversation. Use a campaign for several related conversations. Each campaign has its own landing page, title, description, and optional welcome video.

Your title should tell people what the overall conversation is about. Tips: Keep it short. Aim for 6 words or fewer. Use plain language. Avoid jargon and internal project names. Cover the big picture. Connect all questions in the campaign. Make it inviting. Encourage people to explore and participate. Stay neutral. Don't suggest a preferred outcome. Examples: Envision Marin Reimagining the Civic Center Improving Transportation in Marin

Give people enough context to understand why the questions belong together. Aim for 50–100 words . Include: Why it matters. Explain the purpose of the campaign. What we're asking. Describe the kinds of feedback you're seeking. How it will help. Explain how the County will use what it hears. Tips: Start with the big picture. Don't repeat every question. Be clear about what is open for input. End with an invitation to explore the questions. Previous Ready to start? Next Questions

A good closing recap answers three questions: What did we hear? Share the main ideas and different views. What did we learn? Explain what the feedback tells us. What happens next? Share next steps, decisions, or when people can expect another update.
Look at the ideas, comments, votes, themes, and reports. Identify common interests, different perspectives, and useful suggestions.

Publish a recap that explains: What we asked. Remind people of the purpose. Who participated. Share available participation information. What we heard. Summarize common themes and different views. What happens next. Explain how the County will use the feedback. When to expect updates. Share the next milestone, if known. If you created a campaign, close its questions and share an overall update.

Thank residents and community partners for their time and contributions. The most important part of engagement is closing the loop. People should know their feedback was heard, even when the County cannot act on every idea. Previous Post updates Next Example engagement

This fictional example shows how the parts of an Engage Marin effort work together.

Title: Improving Marin parks Description: Marin's parks bring people together and offer places to play, relax, and enjoy nature. We want to learn how people use these spaces and what could make them better. Explore the questions below and share your ideas. Your feedback will help the County understand community priorities as it plans future park improvements.

Question: How can we make County parks more welcoming? Description: County parks serve people of all ages and backgrounds. We want to hear what works well and what could improve. Share your ideas to help us understand what matters most to park visitors.

Overview County parks give people places to enjoy nature, spend time with family, and connect with their community. We want to learn how people use these spaces and what could make them more welcoming. Why we're asking People visit parks for many reasons. Some come to walk or play. Others come to relax, meet friends, or enjoy nature. We want to hear from people with different needs and experiences. How to participate Share what you enjoy about County parks and what you would change. You can also read other ideas, join discussions, and show support for suggestions. What happens next The County will review the feedback and look for common themes. What we learn will help inform future planning. We'll share a summary of the results when the conversation closes.

Welcome to the conversation! County parks are important places for our community. They give us room to play, relax, and enjoy the outdoors. We want to hear your ideas for making these spaces more welcoming. What do you enjoy most about County parks? What could make your visits better? Share your ideas, read what others have posted, and join the discussion. We welcome different experiences and points of view. We'll follow the conversation and share updates as we learn more. Thank you for helping us make Marin's parks better for everyone.

Example message for a community partner: We're working with Engage Marin to hear ideas about improving County parks. Your experiences and ideas matter. Join the conversation and help us understand what would make these spaces more welcoming for your community.

Thank you for sharing! We've received ideas about park access, trails, play areas, and places to gather. We're reviewing what people have shared and looking for common themes. There's still time to join the conversation. We welcome more ideas and different perspectives.

What we heard Thank you to everyone who shared ideas about County parks. Participants raised several common themes, including access, trails, play areas, and places to gather. What we learned People use parks in different ways. Their feedback helps us better understand what works and where improvements may help. What happens next The County will review these ideas as part of future park planning. We'll share more information as next steps become clear. Thank you for helping shape the future of Marin's parks. Every engagement follows this basic process, whether you ask one question or create a campaign with several questions. 1. Plan Decide what you want to learn, who you want to hear from, and how you'll use their feedback. 2. Create Start a question or campaign. Add an About page, welcome video, and kickoff update. 3. Partner Work with trusted community groups to shape outreach and reach more people. 4. Launch Publish your engagement and invite people through County and partner channels. 5. Monitor Follow ideas, comments, votes, and participation. 6. Organize Set themes to group related ideas and understand what people share. 7. Update Post updates when appropriate to share progress and keep people informed. 8. Close End participation, review results, and publish a recap with next steps.

About Engage Marin Engage Marin is the County of Marin's online community engagement platform. It gives people a simple way to share ideas, give feedback, and help shape County decisions. How it works Engage Marin helps you manage community engagement from start to finish. You can ask one question or bring several related questions together in a campaign. Your commitment Engage Marin provides the tools and support. Your team brings the subject knowledge and stays involved throughout the conversation. Why partners matter Good engagement starts with trust. What to expect Engage Marin makes community engagement easier, but a successful effort still takes planning, outreach, and follow-through. Content Limit Question 10 words or fewer Question description 2–4 sentences You can create a standalone question or add it to a campaign. Each question has its own page, participation settings, updates, themes, and reports.

Your question is the most important part of the conversation. Tips: Short. Aim for 10 words or fewer. Simple. Use plain language. Focused. Ask one question. Open. Invite ideas, not yes/no answers. Neutral. Don't lead people toward a preferred answer. Examples: What transportation improvements would make the biggest difference for you? How can we make County parks more welcoming for everyone? What should we prioritize in next year's budget?

Use 2–4 short sentences to give people enough context to respond. Include: Why it matters. Explain why you're asking. What you're asking. Tell people what feedback you're looking for. How it will help. Explain how the County will use the feedback. Tips: Use plain language. Avoid jargon and explain technical terms. End with an invitation to participate. A welcome video makes the conversation more personal and helps build trust. You can add videos to campaigns and questions.

Content Limit Welcome video length 30–60 seconds Welcome video title 3–8 words Welcome video description 25–50 words Video resolution 1080p Video aspect ratio 16:9 or 1:1 Video file type MP4 Video captions Required, using a reviewed WebVTT (.vtt) file Tips: Keep it short. Aim for 30–60 seconds. Be yourself. Speak naturally and look at the camera. Explain why it matters. Share the purpose and how feedback will help. Invite everyone in. Welcome different views and experiences. End positively. Thank people for sharing their ideas. Avoid large blocks of text in videos. Use spoken words to explain the topic and invite participation.
Resolution: 1080p. Aspect ratio: 16:9 or 1:1. Preferred format: MP4. Captions: Required, using a reviewed WebVTT (.vtt) file. Engage Marin videos are published through the County's YouTube channel.
Keep the introduction title to 3–8 words . Start with an action when possible, clearly state the topic, and focus on the participant.

Aim for 25–50 words in 1–2 short sentences. Include: Who's speaking. Name and title. Why they're inviting participation. Explain the purpose. What people should do. Invite viewers to contribute. Keep it factual and conversational. Don't repeat everything said in the video. Previous About page Next First post

Don't wait until your question is ready to publish. Partners can help you understand what matters to their communities before you finalize the engagement. Ask partners to help: Identify issues and concerns you may have missed. Review questions for clarity. Suggest ways to reach people. Share the invitation through trusted channels. Encourage people to take part. Engage Marin gives partners their own links, logos, and welcome messages. This lets them invite people in their own voice while connecting everyone to the same conversation. Partners do more than share a link. They help turn a County question into a community conversation.
